---
title: "Render In Isolation"
execute:
  eval: false
engine: markdown
---

The first page of our project establishes Quarto as our
human-readable engineering surface. This makes use of our
[Quarto Manual](https://goldenplanetaryhealthlab.github.io/QuartoManual/) workflow.

Quarto has a notable limitation that we're still investigating.
The gist is that we can't seem to have multiple renders running smoothly
on the cluster, causing odd errors that are hard to debug.

Use `scripts/render-isolated` when another Quarto render may be using this
checkout. It stages a private copy of the repository on the node-local
temporary filesystem, so each render owns its own `notebooks/.quarto/_freeze`
directory and Quarto cache. Only a successful rendered site is copied back to
the shared checkout.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm The Render And Publish Boundary"}

Run this script from a checkout with `bash`, `rsync`, `mktemp`, and `quarto`
available on `PATH`. Do not run two publishing renders against the same
checkout at once: the staged renders are independent, but both would still
promote their finished site into the one shared `docs/` directory.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-script-sh file="{{ emit.project_root }}/scripts/render-isolated" mode="0755" title="Materialize The Isolated Render Wrapper"}

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render the Manual in a private staging copy. Forward any arguments to
# `quarto render notebooks`; this avoids contention for notebooks/.quarto/_freeze.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/render-isolated.sh [quarto-render-argument ...]
#
# Example:
#   scripts/render-isolated.sh --profile authoring
set -euo pipefail

script_dir=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
project_dir=$(cd "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
stage_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/quarto-render.XXXXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$stage_dir"' EXIT

# Quarto's Sass cache is a Deno KV database normally kept under ~/.cache.
# Keep all XDG state in the staging directory so concurrent jobs do not share
# that database.
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$stage_dir/xdg-cache"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="$stage_dir/xdg-data"
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$stage_dir/xdg-runtime"
mkdir -p "$XDG_CACHE_HOME" "$XDG_DATA_HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"

# Give this render new Quarto state. Do not copy generated site output or prior
# render state into the staging project: the emit manifest must describe only
# files produced by this render.
rsync -a \
  --exclude '.git' \
  --exclude '.jj' \
  --exclude 'docs' \
  --exclude '.quarto' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/.quarto' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/_site' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/site_libs' \
  "$project_dir/" "$stage_dir/project/"

(
  cd "$stage_dir/project"
  quarto render notebooks "$@"
)

# Quarto-emit records every generated file and its source page in this
# manifest. Promote only those files after a successful render; never copy
# arbitrary staged project state or pipeline outputs back to the checkout.
emit_manifest="$stage_dir/project/.quarto/quarto-emit-manifest.tsv"
stage_project=$(realpath -e "$stage_dir/project")
if [[ -f "$emit_manifest" ]]; then
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r emitted_path source_page; do
    [[ -n "$emitted_path" && -n "$source_page" ]] || continue
    case "$source_page" in
      "$stage_project"/notebooks/*) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing emit manifest source outside notebooks: $source_page" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac

    staged_file=$(realpath -e "$(dirname "$source_page")/$emitted_path") || {
      echo "Generated file listed in manifest is missing: $emitted_path" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    case "$staged_file" in
      "$stage_project"/*) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing emit target outside staged project: $staged_file" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac

    destination="$project_dir/${staged_file#"$stage_project"/}"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
    rsync -a "$staged_file" "$destination"
  done < "$emit_manifest"
fi

# docs/ is this Quarto project's configured output directory. Promote only a
# successful staged render; --delete keeps the published site exact.
rsync -a --delete "$stage_dir/project/docs/" "$project_dir/docs/"
```

:::

Run the generated wrapper from the repository root. Any arguments after the
script name are forwarded to `quarto render notebooks`:

```sh
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
```

## Profiles

Quarto profiles keep the three kinds of work in this project explicit:
`authoring` is the default for reading, editing, and previewing the Manual;
it renders the site without loading the file-emission extension. `emit` loads
that extension and materializes the scripts and configuration described by the
Manual. Both profiles disable code execution completely: rendering and
emission are host-side documentation operations, not scientific computation.

They are separate because these operations have different side effects and
review expectations. An ordinary authoring render should be safe to repeat
without unexpectedly changing generated files or processing data. Emitting
files is an intentional, reviewable synchronization from the Manual to its
derived artifacts.

The isolated wrapper promotes files recorded by Quarto-emit's manifest after a
successful render, so an `emit` render updates the Manual's generated scripts
and configuration in the checkout. It does not run targets or promote arbitrary
data products. Run scientific work separately through the container runner after
reviewing the emitted targets graph.

::: {.manual-explain title="Why Staging Prevents The Freeze Failure"}

At the end of a project render, Quarto prunes its freeze directory. Two
processes pruning the same `notebooks/.quarto/_freeze` tree can race: one sees
entries that the other has already removed, which can surface as `Directory not
empty`. The staged copy gives each render a separate tree, so the prune operation
has no shared mutable directory to remove.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Verify The Generated Wrapper"}

Materialize the script and check its syntax:

```sh
quarto render notebooks --profile emit --no-execute
bash -n scripts/render-isolated
```

Confirm that `scripts/render-isolated` begins with the generated-file
provenance header. The manual page, rather than the generated script, is the
source of truth.

:::
